service.name: After-party entertainment
service.serviceType: Live music and DJs for conference after-parties, gala after-parties and corporate late nights
service.description: After-party entertainment for conferences, galas and company parties in Denver and across Colorado: open-format DJ with a live musician, live band karaoke, soul and R&B band and yacht rock band, on one contract with the venue's load-in window and sound cap settled before the day.

faqs.q: Can the after-party start the moment the program ends?
faqs.a: Yes. The sound system goes up before the doors open, so the band or the DJ is set and checked during the reception, can play dinner at conversation volume if the night wants it, and turns the dance floor on at the emcee's last word, with no changeover the guests can see.

faqs.q: Do we need a second sound system for the after-party?
faqs.a: No. Sound support that's the right size for the venue is included, and a band, the DJ and a live musician over the DJ set all run through the same system on the same contract. A hotel's house system is specified for speeches and won't carry a dance floor, which is why ours comes with the booking.

faqs.q: What does the hotel need to know?
faqs.a: The dock time and the elevator window, the circuits we need, one or two dedicated 20-amp lines depending on the act, the decibel cap and the curfew, and the run of show. Footprints and power by size are on our technical page, written so a hotel's events office can read them without a phone call, and load-in usually runs 45 to 90 minutes depending on size.

faqs.q: Which acts work as an after-party?
faqs.a: The open-format DJ on its own or with a saxophonist or a bassist over the set, live band karaoke when the point is the crowd on stage, the soul and R&B band on a ballroom floor, and the yacht rock band for a crowd that wants to sing every chorus. A DJ can also carry the late set after the band wraps, through the same system and on the same contract.

Yes, and the DJ reads the dance floor from the first song. An open-format set is built for a conference crowd from six cities. Live band karaoke takes requests by definition, with the words on a screen.

faqs.q: How loud can it be, and what about the curfew?
faqs.a: As loud as the venue allows. A hotel's decibel cap and curfew are honoured as written, and we'd like both numbers when we sign the contract so we can build the set under them rather than turning it down on the night. Denver's downtown hotels and the convention-center properties each run their own rules, and we settle them with the events office before the day.
